llm.summary: The Attio skill is mostly coherent, but its setup instructions include direct execution of unverified remote installer scripts, so users should review it before installing.

dimensions.detail: Normal operation uses OOMOL's Attio connector with server-side credential injection, which is proportionate to the purpose; the remote installer path expands local execution risk during setup.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: First-time setup documents curl-to-bash and irm-to-iex installer commands from cli.oomol.com without version pinning, checksum verification, signature verification, or local inspection.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime use is scoped to the oo CLI and tells the agent to inspect live schemas before sending payloads; however, it can affect business CRM records, including deletion, so user confirmation is important.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No bundled persistence, background worker, privilege escalation, or local credential-file access was found in the artifact; any persistence risk would come from the externally fetched installer, not shipped skill code.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's Attio read, create, update, upsert, and delete capabilities fit its stated CRM integration purpose, and write/destructive actions are labeled with confirmation requirements.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust OOMOL and the Attio connector, and avoid running the documented one-line remote installer blindly. Prefer a separately verified, version-pinned oo CLI installation path, review requested Attio scopes, and require explicit approval before any record update, upsert, or delete action.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The cited text describes an Attio identify action for the current token, workspace, and scopes; the artifact says OOMOL injects credentials server-side and does not show local credential-file reading or token theft behavior.
[SC2] unexpected: Installing the oo CLI is purpose-related, but directly piping mutable remote scripts into bash or PowerShell is an overbroad setup mechanism for a skill and lacks integrity safeguards.
[T03] unexpected: The SARIF finding is supported by the artifact at the installer lines: both macOS/Linux and Windows setup commands fetch remote scripts and execute them immediately without verification.
